concepts.name: Binary and radix representation
concepts.gloss: Writing a nonnegative integer as a sequence of digits in base 2 or base 2^b, with carries when digit values overflow.

concepts.name: Two's complement integers
concepts.gloss: The standard fixed-width encoding of signed integers in binary, with addition performed bitwise with carries.

concepts.name: Bitwise XOR and arithmetic mod 2
concepts.gloss: Addition of bits modulo 2, which is exclusive-or, with x + x = 0, so XORing a value twice restores it.

concepts.name: Logarithms and floors/ceilings
concepts.gloss: Base-2 logarithms and the floor and ceiling functions, including the rules for manipulating logarithms in growth rates.

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic and primes
concepts.gloss: Arithmetic on remainders modulo n, greatest common divisors, coprimality, prime numbers and inverses of residues coprime to the modulus.

concepts.name: Roots of unity
concepts.gloss: The n complex solutions of z^n = 1, namely e^{2 pi i k/n}, which lie on the unit circle and form a cyclic group under multiplication.

concepts.name: Vector spaces, subspaces, dimension and rank
concepts.gloss: The core linear algebra notions of vector space, subspace, basis, dimension and the rank of a matrix or linear map.

concepts.name: Matrices and linear operators
concepts.gloss: Matrices as linear maps on finite-dimensional spaces, with products, inverses, diagonal, triangular and permutation matrices and the notion of two operators commuting.

concepts.name: Gaussian elimination and triangular factorization
concepts.gloss: Reducing a matrix by row operations to triangular form, which yields factorizations into triangular factors and solves linear systems.

concepts.name: Orthogonality and inner products
concepts.gloss: The dot product on real or complex coordinate spaces, orthogonal and orthonormal bases, and the orthogonal complement of a subspace.

concepts.name: Norms and the triangle inequality

concepts.name: Permutations and bijections
concepts.gloss: Bijective rearrangements of a finite set of indices, with composition and inverses.

concepts.name: Cartesian products and multi-index arrays
concepts.gloss: Arrays indexed by tuples from a product of finite sets, stored linearly in lexicographic (row-major) order.

concepts.name: Directed acyclic graphs and networks of gates
concepts.gloss: Directed graphs without cycles, and circuits made of gates connected by wires that compute a function of their inputs.

concepts.name: Summation, geometric series and induction
concepts.gloss: Sigma notation, closed forms for geometric series, and proofs by induction on integers.

concepts.name: Rounding to the nearest integer and exactness

concepts.name: Contractions and bilinear contractions

concepts.name: Tensor products of subspaces
concepts.gloss: The space built from two spaces whose dimension is the product of their dimensions, in which operators and bilinear forms act factorwise.

butterfly.name: transform length
butterfly.meaning: The number of positions in the sequence being transformed, a power of two.
butterfly.quote: Here $t$ is the transform length, a power of two.

butterfly.name: input value
butterfly.meaning: The input value at position k of the sequence being transformed.
butterfly.quote: Let $z_k$, for positions $0\le k<t$, be the input values, and let $\omega_t=e^{2\pi i/t}$.

butterfly.name: output index
butterfly.meaning: The index of an output of the transform.
butterfly.quote: The transform is $(F_tz)_m=\frac1t\sum_j z_j\omega_t^{-jm}$, where $m$ is the output index.

butterfly.name: lowest bit
butterfly.meaning: The lowest bit of the output index m.
butterfly.quote: Write $m=2h+b$, where $b\in\{0,1\}$ is the lowest bit of $m$ and $h$ is the remaining index.

butterfly.name: remaining index
butterfly.meaning: The output index m with its lowest bit removed.
butterfly.quote: Write $m=2h+b$, where $b\in\{0,1\}$ is the lowest bit of $m$ and $h$ is the remaining index.

chirp.name: index tuple
chirp.meaning: The tuple of indices (j_1,...,j_d), one per axis, locating an entry of an array.
chirp.quote: Data are arrays indexed by $\boldsymbol j=(j_1,\dots,j_d)$, where $d$ is the number of axes.

chirp.name: axis lengths
chirp.meaning: The tuple (t_1,...,t_d) of axis lengths, where t_i is the even number of entries along axis i.
chirp.quote: The tuple $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$ lists the axis lengths, where $t_i$ is the even number of entries along axis $i$, and $s_i$ is an integer coprime to $t_i$.

chirp.name: coprime multiplier
chirp.meaning: An integer coprime to the axis length t_i.
chirp.quote: The tuple $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$ lists the axis lengths, where $t_i$ is the even number of entries along axis $i$, and $s_i$ is an integer coprime to $t_i$.

chirp.name: normalized transform
chirp.meaning: The normalized multidimensional discrete Fourier transform with axis lengths t.
chirp.quote: The normalized transform $F_{\boldsymbol t}$ is given by $(F_{\boldsymbol t}u)_{\boldsymbol f}=\frac1T\sum_{\boldsymbol k}u_{\boldsymbol k}\exp(-2\pi i\sum_i k_if_i/t_i)$, where $\boldsymbol k$ runs over input positions and $\boldsymbol f=(f_1,\dots,f_d)$ is the frequency labelling an output entry.

chirp.name: input position
chirp.meaning: The index tuple of an input entry.
chirp.quote: The normalized transform $F_{\boldsymbol t}$ is given by $(F_{\boldsymbol t}u)_{\boldsymbol f}=\frac1T\sum_{\boldsymbol k}u_{\boldsymbol k}\exp(-2\pi i\sum_i k_if_i/t_i)$, where $\boldsymbol k$ runs over input positions and $\boldsymbol f=(f_1,\dots,f_d)$ is the frequency labelling an output entry.

chirp.name: frequency
chirp.meaning: The tuple of frequencies labelling an output entry of the transform.
chirp.quote: The normalized transform $F_{\boldsymbol t}$ is given by $(F_{\boldsymbol t}u)_{\boldsymbol f}=\frac1T\sum_{\boldsymbol k}u_{\boldsymbol k}\exp(-2\pi i\sum_i k_if_i/t_i)$, where $\boldsymbol k$ runs over input positions and $\boldsymbol f=(f_1,\dots,f_d)$ is the frequency labelling an output entry.

chirp.name: target permutation
chirp.meaning: The permutation reordering the output so that position j holds the entry of frequency (-s_i j_i)_i.
chirp.quote: The target permutation $Q$ reorders the output so that position $\boldsymbol j$ holds the entry of frequency $(-s_ij_i)_i$.

chirp.name: chirp
chirp.meaning: The chirp, a phase quadratic in the index.
chirp.quote: Define the chirp $a_{\boldsymbol j}=\exp\left(-\pi i\sum_{i=1}^d s_ij_i^2/t_i\right)$, a phase quadratic in the index, and let $\overline a$ be its complex conjugate.

conjecture.name: bit length
conjecture.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two integers being multiplied.
conjecture.quote: The Schönhage–Strassen optimality conjecture is the claim that $n\log n$ is the best possible order of growth for the time to multiply two integers, where $n$ is the number of bits in each; it is the statement that the main result of this wiki disproves.

conjecture.name: power saving
conjecture.meaning: A fixed positive constant, the amount by which the exponent of the logarithm is lowered.
conjecture.quote: Its running time is $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$, where $\kappa>0$ is a fixed constant, the amount by which the exponent of the logarithm is lowered.

contraction-maps.name: linear map
contraction-maps.meaning: A linear map whose norm bound is being defined.
contraction-maps.quote: A linear map $L$ is a *contraction* if $\|Lu\|\le\|u\|$ for every $u$.

contraction-maps.name: bilinear map
contraction-maps.meaning: A map linear in each of its two operands.
contraction-maps.quote: A map $\mathcal M(f,g)$ that is linear in each operand $f$ and $g$ separately is a *bilinear contraction* if $\|\mathcal M(f,g)\|\le\|f\|\,\|g\|$.

contraction-maps.name: computed input
contraction-maps.meaning: The computed input that replaces the exact input u.
contraction-maps.quote: Suppose a computed input $u'$ replaces the exact input $u$.

contraction-maps.name: computed first operand
contraction-maps.quote: For a bilinear contraction, replace operands $f,g$ by $f',g'$.

contraction-maps.name: computed second operand
contraction-maps.quote: For a bilinear contraction, replace operands $f,g$ by $f',g'$.

contraction-maps.name: normalized transform
contraction-maps.meaning: The normalized discrete Fourier transform on sequences of q entries.
contraction-maps.quote: where $F_q$ is the transform on sequences of $q$ entries.

contraction-maps.name: first operand
contraction-maps.meaning: The first operand of the bilinear map.
contraction-maps.quote: A map $\mathcal M(f,g)$ that is linear in each operand $f$ and $g$ separately is a *bilinear contraction* if $\|\mathcal M(f,g)\|\le\|f\|\,\|g\|$.

contraction-maps.name: second operand
contraction-maps.meaning: The second operand of the bilinear map.
contraction-maps.quote: A map $\mathcal M(f,g)$ that is linear in each operand $f$ and $g$ separately is a *bilinear contraction* if $\|\mathcal M(f,g)\|\le\|f\|\,\|g\|$.

controlled-shifts.name: prime radix
controlled-shifts.meaning: The radix of the stored digits, a prime (not a sequence length).
controlled-shifts.quote: Fix a prime $q$, the radix of the stored digits; this $q$ is a prime radix, not a sequence length as on the cyclic convolution and discrete Fourier transform pages.

controlled-shifts.name: field digit count
controlled-shifts.meaning: The number of base-q digits of a field.
controlled-shifts.quote: Let $b\ge1$ be the number of base-$q$ digits of a field; this $b$ is not the lowest bit of an output index as on the butterfly page.

controlled-shifts.name: field value count
controlled-shifts.meaning: The number of values a field can take.
controlled-shifts.quote: Put $Q=q^b$, the number of values a field can take.

controlled-shifts.name: field value
controlled-shifts.meaning: The value of the target field, an integer from 0 to Q-1 (not the ring variable).
controlled-shifts.quote: The target field has value $y\in\{0,\dots,Q-1\}$; here $y$ is a field value, not the ring variable.

controlled-shifts.name: offset
controlled-shifts.meaning: The offset added to the target field, prepared from the control values.
controlled-shifts.quote: where $a$ is the offset prepared from the control values; this $a$ is not a bank index.

controlled-shifts.name: suffix digit count
controlled-shifts.meaning: The number of digits following the target field.
controlled-shifts.quote: Let $B$ be the number of digits that follow the target; this $B$ is not the number of entries per row on the stream-operations page.

controlled-shifts.name: scaling multiplier
controlled-shifts.meaning: A fixed positive integer prime to q by which the field is multiplied.
controlled-shifts.quote: Let $c$ be a fixed positive integer prime to $q$.

controlled-shifts.name: wrap count
controlled-shifts.meaning: The number of times cy wraps past Q.
controlled-shifts.quote: where $j=\lfloor cy/Q\rfloor$ is the number of times $cy$ wraps past $Q$; this $j$ is not a digit value as on the stream-operations page.

controlled-shifts.name: scaled position
controlled-shifts.meaning: The position cy - jQ to which the block at position y is sent.
controlled-shifts.quote: The map $y\mapsto cy \pmod Q$ sends the block at position $y$ to position $y'=cy-jQ$, where $j=\lfloor cy/Q\rfloor$ is the number of times $cy$ wraps past $Q$; this $j$ is not a digit value as on the stream-operations page.

controlled-shifts.name: unit denominator
controlled-shifts.meaning: The positive integer denominator of a rational unit, prime to q.
controlled-shifts.quote: A rational unit is a signed ratio $c/c'$ of positive integers $c,c'$ both prime to $q$.

convolution.name: sequence length
convolution.meaning: The number of entries in each of the two sequences being convolved.
convolution.quote: For two sequences $f,g$ indexed by $\mathbb Z/q\mathbb Z$, where $q$ is the number of entries in each sequence, the cyclic convolution is

convolution.name: axis count
convolution.meaning: The number of axes of an array, counting the d-1 cyclic axes plus the coefficient axis.
convolution.quote: The algorithm uses arrays with $d-1$ cyclic axes, so $d$ counts the cyclic axes plus the coefficient axis, and $t_i$ is the length of cyclic axis $i$.

convolution.name: axis length
convolution.meaning: The length of cyclic axis i.
convolution.quote: The algorithm uses arrays with $d-1$ cyclic axes, so $d$ counts the cyclic axes plus the coefficient axis, and $t_i$ is the length of cyclic axis $i$.

convolution.name: address count
convolution.meaning: The number of cyclic addresses of an array, the product of the axis lengths.
convolution.quote: Let $M=\prod_{i<d}t_i$ be the number of cyclic addresses, and $T=rM$ the total number of complex coefficients in an array.

convolution.name: coefficient count
convolution.meaning: The total number of complex coefficients in an array.
convolution.quote: Let $M=\prod_{i<d}t_i$ be the number of cyclic addresses, and $T=rM$ the total number of complex coefficients in an array.

cost-accounting.name: volume
cost-accounting.meaning: The number of stored bits of the T coefficients of p bits, equal to Tp and Theta(n); not the larger label of the subspace-label pages.
cost-accounting.quote: Let $V=Tp=\Theta(n)$ be the volume, the number of stored bits of $T$ coefficients of $p$ bits (a volume here, not the larger label of the subspace-label pages).

cost-accounting.name: margin
cost-accounting.meaning: The distance below one of the exponent of p in the i-th dominant normalized cost, so the cost is p^{1-g_i}.
cost-accounting.quote: Dividing by $V$, seven operations dominate, each a power $p^{1-g_i}$ with margin $g_i>0$ below one (a margin, not a guard value).

cost-accounting.name: visit exponent
cost-accounting.meaning: A fixed exponent such that the recursions make at most p^A visits; not the shear matrix or a space of earlier pages.
cost-accounting.quote: Fix an exponent $A$ with at most $p^A$ visits in total, and an exponent $C$ with descriptor setup of at most $p^C$ steps per visit (here $A$ and $C$ are exponents, not the shear matrix, ambient spaces, two-point kernel or selection map of earlier pages).

cost-accounting.name: setup exponent
cost-accounting.meaning: A fixed exponent such that descriptor setup takes at most p^C steps per visit; not the two-point kernel or selection map of earlier pages.
cost-accounting.quote: Fix an exponent $A$ with at most $p^A$ visits in total, and an exponent $C$ with descriptor setup of at most $p^C$ steps per visit (here $A$ and $C$ are exponents, not the shear matrix, ambient spaces, two-point kernel or selection map of earlier pages).

cost-accounting.name: call volume
cost-accounting.meaning: The volume of one packed change of basis.
cost-accounting.quote: Let $V_{\rm call}$ be the volume of one packed change of basis.

crt-map.name: axis count
crt-map.meaning: The number of prime cyclic axes, with no coefficient axis counted.
crt-map.quote: Let $d$ be the number of prime cyclic axes (unlike on the cyclic-convolution page, no coefficient axis is counted), $i$ index them, and $s_1,\dots,s_d$ be pairwise coprime axis lengths (these $s_i$ are unrelated to the chirp page's multipliers).

crt-map.name: axis length
crt-map.meaning: The length of prime cyclic axis i; the s_i are pairwise coprime.
crt-map.quote: Let $d$ be the number of prime cyclic axes (unlike on the cyclic-convolution page, no coefficient axis is counted), $i$ index them, and $s_1,\dots,s_d$ be pairwise coprime axis lengths (these $s_i$ are unrelated to the chirp page's multipliers).

crt-map.name: prefix product
crt-map.meaning: The product of the axis lengths s_j with j<i.
crt-map.quote: Let $P_i=\prod_{j<i}s_j$ be the product of the lengths $s_j$ of the axes $j$ before axis $i$, and $\mu_i=P_i^{-1}\pmod{s_i}$.

crt-map.name: coordinate exponent
crt-map.meaning: The inverse of P_i modulo s_i, the exponent of x_i in the image of x.
crt-map.quote: Let $P_i=\prod_{j<i}s_j$ be the product of the lengths $s_j$ of the axes $j$ before axis $i$, and $\mu_i=P_i^{-1}\pmod{s_i}$.

crt-map.name: address map
crt-map.meaning: The ring isomorphism sending x to the product of x_i^{mu_i}.
crt-map.quote: Define $\Phi:\mathbb C[x]/(x^S-1)\to\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_i^{s_i}-1)$ by $x\mapsto\prod_i x_i^{\mu_i}$, with one variable $x_i$ per axis.

crt-map.name: axis variable
crt-map.meaning: The variable of axis i in the multi-axis ring.
crt-map.quote: Define $\Phi:\mathbb C[x]/(x^S-1)\to\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_i^{s_i}-1)$ by $x\mapsto\prod_i x_i^{\mu_i}$, with one variable $x_i$ per axis.

crt-map.name: coefficient index
crt-map.meaning: A single coefficient index, an exponent of x; not an output index tuple as on the multidimensional-transform page.
crt-map.quote: The letter $k$ changes meaning here: it is a single coefficient index, an exponent of $x$, not an output index tuple as on the multidimensional-transform page.

crt-map.name: mixed-radix digit
crt-map.meaning: The digit of k of weight P_j, with 0<=a_j<s_j.
crt-map.quote: Write $k=\sum_ja_jP_j$ in mixed radix, with digits $0\le a_j<s_j$.

crt-map.name: digit index
crt-map.meaning: The index of an axis before axis i, in the product defining P_i, and later the index of a mixed-radix digit.
crt-map.quote: Let $P_i=\prod_{j<i}s_j$ be the product of the lengths $s_j$ of the axes $j$ before axis $i$, and $\mu_i=P_i^{-1}\pmod{s_i}$.

crt-map.name: axis coordinate
crt-map.quote: The axis-$i$ coordinate $b_i$ of $\Phi(x^k)$ is $\mu_ik\bmod s_i$.

crt-map.name: address bits
crt-map.meaning: The number of address bits of an axis of length r.
crt-map.quote: Pad axis $i$ with zero records to a length $t_i$, a power of two with $r/2\le t_i\le r$, where $r=2^\ell$ is the record length, so $\ell$ is the number of address bits of an axis of length $r$.

crt-map.name: padded record count
crt-map.meaning: The number of padded records, the product of the padded axis lengths t_i.
crt-map.quote: Let $T=\prod_it_i$ be the number of padded records, each of $O(p)$ bits.

crt-map.name: interchange exponent
crt-map.meaning: A fixed exponent below 1 in the chunk-interchange cost.
crt-map.quote: Let $V=Tp$ be the stream volume and $\tau<1$ a fixed exponent.

crt-map.name: axis index
crt-map.meaning: The index of a prime cyclic axis, from 1 to d.
crt-map.quote: Let $d$ be the number of prime cyclic axes (unlike on the cyclic-convolution page, no coefficient axis is counted), $i$ index them, and $s_1,\dots,s_d$ be pairwise coprime axis lengths (these $s_i$ are unrelated to the chirp page's multipliers).

crt-map.name: padded axis length
crt-map.meaning: The length of axis i after zero padding, a power of two between r/2 and r.
crt-map.quote: Pad axis $i$ with zero records to a length $t_i$, a power of two with $r/2\le t_i\le r$, where $r=2^\ell$ is the record length, so $\ell$ is the number of address bits of an axis of length $r$.

dft.name: sequence length
dft.meaning: The number of entries of a sequence.
dft.quote: Let $q\ge 1$ be the number of entries of a sequence, and let $u=(u_0,\dots,u_{q-1})$ be a sequence of $q$ complex numbers, with subscripts taken modulo $q$.

dft.name: input sequence
dft.meaning: A sequence of q complex numbers to be transformed.
dft.quote: Let $q\ge 1$ be the number of entries of a sequence, and let $u=(u_0,\dots,u_{q-1})$ be a sequence of $q$ complex numbers, with subscripts taken modulo $q$.

dft.name: primitive root
dft.meaning: The primitive q-th root of unity e^{2\pi i/q}.
dft.quote: Writing $\omega = e^{2\pi i/q}$ for the primitive $q$-th root of unity, the weights are the powers $\omega^{-jk}$.

exchange-network.name: first data bank
exchange-network.meaning: One of the two data banks, with entries X_a.
exchange-network.quote: There are two data banks $X=(X_a)$ and $Y=(Y_a)$, indexed by $a\in\mathcal T^3$ ($a$ here is a triple of triples, not a shift exponent).

exchange-network.name: second data bank
exchange-network.meaning: The other data bank, with entries Y_a.
exchange-network.quote: There are two data banks $X=(X_a)$ and $Y=(Y_a)$, indexed by $a\in\mathcal T^3$ ($a$ here is a triple of triples, not a shift exponent).

exchange-network.name: bank index
exchange-network.meaning: A triple of three-element subsets of [h] indexing the entries of the banks.
exchange-network.quote: There are two data banks $X=(X_a)$ and $Y=(Y_a)$, indexed by $a\in\mathcal T^3$ ($a$ here is a triple of triples, not a shift exponent).

exchange-network.name: ground-set size
exchange-network.meaning: The size of the ground set [h] whose three-element subsets index the banks.
exchange-network.quote: Fix the ground-set size $h=100$ and write $[h]=\{1,\dots,h\}$.

exchange-network.name: triple set
exchange-network.meaning: The set of three-element subsets of [h].
exchange-network.quote: Let $\mathcal T$ be the set of three-element subsets of $[h]$, so that $v=\binom h3=161700$ counts them.

exchange-network.name: number of triples
exchange-network.meaning: The number of three-element subsets of [h].
exchange-network.quote: Let $\mathcal T$ be the set of three-element subsets of $[h]$, so that $v=\binom h3=161700$ counts them.

exchange-network.name: bank size
exchange-network.meaning: The number of values in each data bank.
exchange-network.quote: Set $N=v^3=4227952113000000$ for the size of each bank, and $m=h^3=1000000$ for the dimension of the label space used later.

exchange-network.name: label-space dimension
exchange-network.meaning: The dimension of the label space used on later pages.
exchange-network.quote: Set $N=v^3=4227952113000000$ for the size of each bank, and $m=h^3=1000000$ for the dimension of the label space used later.

exchange-network.name: invocation count
exchange-network.meaning: The number of invocations over all three stages.
exchange-network.quote: A stage covers all $v^2$ choices of the other two coordinates, each with its own invocation and scratch wires, so there are $I=3v^2=78440670000$ invocations.

exchange-network.name: bit neighbour count
exchange-network.meaning: The number of neighbours of a fixed triple in the bit construction.
exchange-network.quote: A triple has $z_{\rm b}=3\binom{97}{2}=13968$ neighbours in the bit construction

exchange-network.name: complex neighbour count
exchange-network.meaning: The number of neighbours of a fixed triple in the complex construction.
exchange-network.quote: It has $z_{\rm c}=\binom{97}{3}+3\cdot97=147731$ neighbours in the complex construction (intersection zero plus two)

exchange-network.name: bit central wires
exchange-network.meaning: The number of central wires per invocation in the bit network.
exchange-network.quote: There are $c_{\rm b}=100$ central wires per invocation in the bit network and $c_{\rm c}=101$ in the complex one.

exchange-network.name: complex central wires
exchange-network.meaning: The number of central wires per invocation in the complex network.
exchange-network.quote: There are $c_{\rm b}=100$ central wires per invocation in the bit network and $c_{\rm c}=101$ in the complex one.

exchange-network.name: bit wire count
exchange-network.meaning: The total number of wires in the bit network.
exchange-network.quote: The bit network has $W_{\rm b}=2N+I(vz_{\rm b}+c_{\rm b})=177176569091445000000$ wires

exchange-network.name: complex wire count
exchange-network.meaning: The total number of wires in the complex network.
exchange-network.quote: The complex network has $W_{\rm c}=2N+I(vz_{\rm c}+c_{\rm c})=1873807244643542670000$ wires

fixed-point.name: fractional bits
fixed-point.meaning: The number of fractional bits of the grid on which stored values lie.
fixed-point.quote: Let $p$ be the number of fractional bits, so stored values lie on the grid $2^{-p}\mathbb Z[i]$.

fixed-point.name: depth
fixed-point.meaning: The number of operations in sequence since the layer began that produced a value.
fixed-point.quote: Let a value computed with $k$ operations in sequence since the layer began be said to have depth $k$.

fixed-point.name: reserved extra bits
fixed-point.meaning: The number of extra bits reserved, at least the maximal depth reached in the layer.
fixed-point.quote: Let $\Delta$ be the number of extra bits reserved, at least the maximal depth reached in the layer.

fixed-point.name: truncation
fixed-point.meaning: The truncation that drops the bits below 2^{-p} in each real and imaginary part, returning a record to the p-bit grid.
fixed-point.quote: The truncation $Q_p$ drops the bits below $2^{-p}$ in each real and imaginary part, returning the record to the $p$-bit grid, with error below $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$ per complex coefficient.

frequency-order.name: round count
frequency-order.meaning: The number of rounds of the transform, a=log_2 t.
frequency-order.quote: put $a=\log_2t$, the number of rounds (here $a$ changes meaning)

frequency-order.name: output index
frequency-order.meaning: The position of an output of the transform.
frequency-order.quote: with input positions $k$ and output index $j$ (here $j$ changes meaning: it is the position of an output of the transform)

frequency-order.name: completed rounds
frequency-order.meaning: The number of rounds completed so far.
frequency-order.quote: After $s$ rounds, $s$ being the number of completed rounds, slots $a-1,\dots,a-s$ hold frequency bits $0,\dots,s-1$ and the rest index a sequence of length $t/2^s$; the next round writes bit $s$ into slot $a-1-s$.

frequency-order.name: bit-reversal permutation
frequency-order.meaning: The permutation moving the entry at j to rev_a(j).
frequency-order.quote: Let $B_t$ be the permutation moving the entry at $j$ to $\operatorname{rev}_a(j)$

frequency-order.name: parallel butterfly
frequency-order.meaning: The parallel butterfly applying H_0 on every participating axis in one round.
frequency-order.quote: With several axes, indexed by $i$, a round applies $H_0$ on every participating axis, and $\mathcal H$ denotes this one parallel butterfly.

frequency-order.name: recordwise monomial
frequency-order.meaning: The recordwise operation multiplying each record by y^E.
frequency-order.quote: Twiddles group into one monomial $J_E$, the recordwise operation multiplying the record by $y^E$, where $E$ depends on the address, not coefficients:

gaussian-resampling.name: source length
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The length of the Fourier transform being re-expressed, coprime to t.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Gaussian resampling expresses a Fourier transform of length $s$, the source length, through one of a nearby larger length $t$ (a power of two there), so that only power-of-two transforms need a fast algorithm.

gaussian-resampling.name: transform length
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The larger length, a power of two, of the transform through which the length-s transform is expressed.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Gaussian resampling expresses a Fourier transform of length $s$, the source length, through one of a nearby larger length $t$ (a power of two there), so that only power-of-two transforms need a fast algorithm.

gaussian-resampling.name: width parameter
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The integer width parameter of the Gaussian weights, with 2<=alpha<sqrt p.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Let $s<t<2^p$ be coprime integers, where $p>100$ counts the fractional bits of each real and imaginary component, and let $\alpha$, the width parameter of the Gaussian weights below, be an integer with $2\le\alpha<\sqrt p$.

gaussian-resampling.name: relative gap
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The relative gap t/s-1 between the target and source lengths.

gaussian-resampling.name: coordinate index
gaussian-resampling.quote: Several letters are reused here with new meanings: $j$ and $k$ are single coordinate indices, not index tuples as on the multidimensional-transform page.

gaussian-resampling.name: coordinate index
gaussian-resampling.quote: Several letters are reused here with new meanings: $j$ and $k$ are single coordinate indices, not index tuples as on the multidimensional-transform page.

gaussian-resampling.name: nearest coordinate
gaussian-resampling.quote: To undo $\mathsf T$, let $q_j$ be the integer nearest $tj/s$ and $\beta_j=tj/s-q_j$.

gaussian-resampling.name: rounding offset
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The signed distance tj/s-q_j from tj/s to the nearest integer.
gaussian-resampling.quote: To undo $\mathsf T$, let $q_j$ be the integer nearest $tj/s$ and $\beta_j=tj/s-q_j$.

gaussian-resampling.name: Neumann error
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The map N-I, whose norm is small.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Let $E=N-I$ and $K=\lceil p/(\alpha^2\theta)\rceil$, the number of series terms kept.

gaussian-resampling.name: series term count
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The number of terms of the Neumann series that are kept.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Let $E=N-I$ and $K=\lceil p/(\alpha^2\theta)\rceil$, the number of series terms kept.

hvdh-multiplier.name: factor bit length
hvdh-multiplier.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two integers given to the established multiplier.
hvdh-multiplier.quote: The established multiplier is the earlier Harvey–van der Hoeven algorithm, which multiplies two integers of $N$ bits each in $O(N\log N)$ time (this $N$ is not the bank size of the exchange network); the new algorithm calls it as an ordinary subroutine for the integer products it cannot avoid.

matrix-shear.name: field base
matrix-shear.meaning: A fixed odd prime, the base of the digits.
matrix-shear.quote: Here $q$ is a fixed odd prime, the base of the digits, not a sequence length.

matrix-shear.name: digits per field
matrix-shear.meaning: The number of base-q digits in one field.
matrix-shear.quote: Here $b$ is the number of base-$q$ digits in one field, not the lowest bit of an index.

matrix-shear.name: rank

matrix-shear.quote: Here $a$ is the rank of $A$, not an offset added to a field.

matrix-shear.name: fields per group
matrix-shear.meaning: The number of fields in each of the groups H and D.
matrix-shear.quote: Let $H=(H_1,\dots,H_m)$ and $D=(D_1,\dots,D_m)$ be two groups of fields, $H$ before $D$, where $m$ is the number of fields in each group ($m$ counts fields here; it is not an output index).

multidim-transform.name: axis index
multidim-transform.meaning: The index of an axis of the array, from 1 to d.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $d$ be the number of axes, $i$ an axis index with $1\le i\le d$, and $q_i$ the number of positions along axis $i$, so $\boldsymbol q=(q_1,\dots,q_d)$.

multidim-transform.name: axis position count
multidim-transform.meaning: The number of positions along axis i.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $d$ be the number of axes, $i$ an axis index with $1\le i\le d$, and $q_i$ the number of positions along axis $i$, so $\boldsymbol q=(q_1,\dots,q_d)$.

multidim-transform.name: index tuple
multidim-transform.meaning: The tuple of coordinates (j_1,...,j_d) of an entry of the array.
multidim-transform.quote: An entry of the array $u$ has an index tuple $j=(j_1,\dots,j_d)$ with $0\le j_i<q_i$.

multidim-transform.name: output index tuple
multidim-transform.meaning: An output index tuple shaped like j.
multidim-transform.quote:
With $k$ an output index tuple shaped like $j$,
$$(F_{\boldsymbol q}u)_k=\frac1{\prod_i q_i}\sum_j u_j\,e^{-2\pi i\sum_i j_ik_i/q_i}.$$

multidim-transform.name: axis operator
multidim-transform.meaning: An operator on sequences of length q_i, applied to every line along axis i.
multidim-transform.quote: For operators $G_i$ on sequences of length $q_i$, the tensor product $\bigotimes_i G_i$ applies each $G_i$ to every line along axis $i$.

multidim-transform.name: time-bound slack
multidim-transform.meaning: A fixed constant with 0<delta<1/8 that sets the slack in the exponent 3/2+delta of p in the time bound.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $p$ be the number of fractional bits of the stored values, $\alpha$ an integer resampling parameter with $2\le\alpha<\sqrt p$, and $\delta$ a fixed constant with $0<\delta<1/8$ that sets the slack in the exponent $3/2+\delta$ of $p$ in the time bound.

multidim-transform.name: resampling parameter
multidim-transform.meaning: An integer resampling parameter with 2<=alpha<sqrt p.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $p$ be the number of fractional bits of the stored values, $\alpha$ an integer resampling parameter with $2\le\alpha<\sqrt p$, and $\delta$ a fixed constant with $0<\delta<1/8$ that sets the slack in the exponent $3/2+\delta$ of $p$ in the time bound.

multidim-transform.name: source lengths
multidim-transform.meaning: The tuple of source axis lengths (s_1,...,s_d).
multidim-transform.quote: Let $\boldsymbol s=(s_1,\dots,s_d)$ and $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$ be the source and padded axis lengths, $\gamma=2d\alpha^2$ the total exponent of the scalar, and, with $R$ here not the scalar ring, $R=\bigotimes_iP_{s_i}$, $Q=\bigotimes_iP_{t_i}$, $\mathcal A=\bigotimes_iA_i$, $\mathcal B_0=\bigotimes_iB_{0,i}$:

multidim-transform.meaning: The tuple of padded power-of-two axis lengths (t_1,...,t_d).
multidim-transform.quote: Let $\boldsymbol s=(s_1,\dots,s_d)$ and $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$ be the source and padded axis lengths, $\gamma=2d\alpha^2$ the total exponent of the scalar, and, with $R$ here not the scalar ring, $R=\bigotimes_iP_{s_i}$, $Q=\bigotimes_iP_{t_i}$, $\mathcal A=\bigotimes_iA_i$, $\mathcal B_0=\bigotimes_iB_{0,i}$:

multidim-transform.name: scalar exponent
multidim-transform.meaning: The total exponent 2d alpha^2 of the power of two multiplying the tensored identity.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $\boldsymbol s=(s_1,\dots,s_d)$ and $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$ be the source and padded axis lengths, $\gamma=2d\alpha^2$ the total exponent of the scalar, and, with $R$ here not the scalar ring, $R=\bigotimes_iP_{s_i}$, $Q=\bigotimes_iP_{t_i}$, $\mathcal A=\bigotimes_iA_i$, $\mathcal B_0=\bigotimes_iB_{0,i}$:

multidim-transform.name: source permutation
multidim-transform.meaning: The tensor product of the source index permutations P_{s_i}; here not the scalar ring.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $\boldsymbol s=(s_1,\dots,s_d)$ and $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$ be the source and padded axis lengths, $\gamma=2d\alpha^2$ the total exponent of the scalar, and, with $R$ here not the scalar ring, $R=\bigotimes_iP_{s_i}$, $Q=\bigotimes_iP_{t_i}$, $\mathcal A=\bigotimes_iA_i$, $\mathcal B_0=\bigotimes_iB_{0,i}$:

multidim-transform.name: padded permutation
multidim-transform.meaning: The tensor product of the index permutations P_{t_i}.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $\boldsymbol s=(s_1,\dots,s_d)$ and $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$ be the source and padded axis lengths, $\gamma=2d\alpha^2$ the total exponent of the scalar, and, with $R$ here not the scalar ring, $R=\bigotimes_iP_{s_i}$, $Q=\bigotimes_iP_{t_i}$, $\mathcal A=\bigotimes_iA_i$, $\mathcal B_0=\bigotimes_iB_{0,i}$:

multidim-transform.name: input map
multidim-transform.meaning: The tensor product of the one-dimensional input maps A_i.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $\boldsymbol s=(s_1,\dots,s_d)$ and $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$ be the source and padded axis lengths, $\gamma=2d\alpha^2$ the total exponent of the scalar, and, with $R$ here not the scalar ring, $R=\bigotimes_iP_{s_i}$, $Q=\bigotimes_iP_{t_i}$, $\mathcal A=\bigotimes_iA_i$, $\mathcal B_0=\bigotimes_iB_{0,i}$:

multidim-transform.name: output map
multidim-transform.meaning: The tensor product of the one-dimensional output maps B_{0,i}.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $\boldsymbol s=(s_1,\dots,s_d)$ and $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$ be the source and padded axis lengths, $\gamma=2d\alpha^2$ the total exponent of the scalar, and, with $R$ here not the scalar ring, $R=\bigotimes_iP_{s_i}$, $Q=\bigotimes_iP_{t_i}$, $\mathcal A=\bigotimes_iA_i$, $\mathcal B_0=\bigotimes_iB_{0,i}$:

multidim-transform.name: source axis permutation
multidim-transform.meaning: The index permutation of source axis i.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $P_{s_i}$ and $P_{t_i}$ be the index permutations of the source and padded axes, and $A_i$ and $B_{0,i}$ the linear input and output maps of axis $i$.

multidim-transform.name: padded axis permutation
multidim-transform.meaning: The index permutation of padded axis i.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $P_{s_i}$ and $P_{t_i}$ be the index permutations of the source and padded axes, and $A_i$ and $B_{0,i}$ the linear input and output maps of axis $i$.

multidim-transform.name: axis input map
multidim-transform.meaning: The linear input map of axis i.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $P_{s_i}$ and $P_{t_i}$ be the index permutations of the source and padded axes, and $A_i$ and $B_{0,i}$ the linear input and output maps of axis $i$.

multidim-transform.name: axis output map
multidim-transform.meaning: The linear output map of axis i.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $P_{s_i}$ and $P_{t_i}$ be the index permutations of the source and padded axes, and $A_i$ and $B_{0,i}$ the linear input and output maps of axis $i$.

multidim-transform.name: axis transform
multidim-transform.meaning: The one-dimensional normalized discrete Fourier transform of length q_i.
multidim-transform.quote: Here $F_{q_i}$ is the one-dimensional normalized [Discrete Fourier transform](dft.md) of length $q_i$, and $F_{\boldsymbol q}:=\bigotimes_iF_{q_i}$ is the tensor product of these.

multidim-transform.name: multidimensional transform
multidim-transform.meaning: The tensor product of the axis transforms F_{q_i}.
multidim-transform.quote: Here $F_{q_i}$ is the one-dimensional normalized [Discrete Fourier transform](dft.md) of length $q_i$, and $F_{\boldsymbol q}:=\bigotimes_iF_{q_i}$ is the tensor product of these.

multidim-transform.name: axis operator X
multidim-transform.meaning: An operator on axis i.
multidim-transform.quote: Operators compose axis by axis, so $(\bigotimes_i X_i)(\bigotimes_i Y_i)=\bigotimes_i X_iY_i$ for operators $X_i,Y_i$ on axis $i$, and the scalars multiply.

multidim-transform.name: axis operator Y
multidim-transform.meaning: An operator on axis i.
multidim-transform.quote: Operators compose axis by axis, so $(\bigotimes_i X_i)(\bigotimes_i Y_i)=\bigotimes_i X_iY_i$ for operators $X_i,Y_i$ on axis $i$, and the scalars multiply.

multiplication-algorithm.name: digit width
multiplication-algorithm.meaning: The number of bits in one radix digit.
multiplication-algorithm.quote: It takes its sizes from [Parameter and prime-length choice](parameter-choice.md): $b=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$ is the digit width (the number of bits in one radix digit, not the digit count of a field, a lowest bit, a count of leftover bits or a kernel coefficient), $p=6b$ is the number of fractional bits, $s_i$ are distinct odd prime axis lengths with product $S$, and $t_i$ are power-of-two axis lengths with product $T$.

multiplication-algorithm.name: radix digit
multiplication-algorithm.meaning: The j-th radix-2^b digit of an input.
multiplication-algorithm.quote: Each input splits into $q=\lceil n/b\rceil$ radix-$2^b$ digits $a_j$, and the product is their convolution modulo $x^S-1$, as in [Multiplication as radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-reduction.md).

multiplication-algorithm.name: source transform
multiplication-algorithm.meaning: The discrete Fourier transform on the prime axes s_i, normalized by 1/S.
multiplication-algorithm.quote: Let $F_{\boldsymbol s}$ be the discrete Fourier transform on the axes $s_i$, normalized by $1/S$. $F_{\boldsymbol s}^+$ is the same with the opposite sign in the exponent, and $F_{\boldsymbol t}$ is the transform on the axes $t_i$, normalized by $1/T$.

multiplication-algorithm.name: opposite source transform
multiplication-algorithm.meaning: The source transform with the opposite sign in the exponent.
multiplication-algorithm.quote: Let $F_{\boldsymbol s}$ be the discrete Fourier transform on the axes $s_i$, normalized by $1/S$. $F_{\boldsymbol s}^+$ is the same with the opposite sign in the exponent, and $F_{\boldsymbol t}$ is the transform on the axes $t_i$, normalized by $1/T$.

multiplication-algorithm.name: computed chirp
multiplication-algorithm.meaning: The grid approximation of the chirp a.
multiplication-algorithm.quote: The computed version uses an approximation $\widetilde a$ of $a$ and truncation $Q_p$ to $p$ fractional bits.

multiplication-algorithm.name: first-phase operand
multiplication-algorithm.meaning: The data operand after the first phase of the computed chirp transform.
multiplication-algorithm.quote: It forms the operand $x_0=Q_p(\overline{\widetilde a}\cdot x)$ after the first phase, then $y_0=\widetilde{\mathcal M}_{\mathbb C}(\widetilde a,x_0)$, the computed convolution, and returns $\widetilde{\mathscr C}(x)=Q_p(\overline{\widetilde a}\cdot y_0)$.

multiplication-algorithm.name: chirp convolution
multiplication-algorithm.meaning: The computed convolution of the approximate chirp with the data operand.
multiplication-algorithm.quote: It forms the operand $x_0=Q_p(\overline{\widetilde a}\cdot x)$ after the first phase, then $y_0=\widetilde{\mathcal M}_{\mathbb C}(\widetilde a,x_0)$, the computed convolution, and returns $\widetilde{\mathscr C}(x)=Q_p(\overline{\widetilde a}\cdot y_0)$.

multiplication-algorithm.name: computed convolution
multiplication-algorithm.meaning: The computed normalized complex cyclic convolution.
multiplication-algorithm.quote: It forms the operand $x_0=Q_p(\overline{\widetilde a}\cdot x)$ after the first phase, then $y_0=\widetilde{\mathcal M}_{\mathbb C}(\widetilde a,x_0)$, the computed convolution, and returns $\widetilde{\mathscr C}(x)=Q_p(\overline{\widetilde a}\cdot y_0)$.

multiplication-algorithm.name: source permutation
multiplication-algorithm.meaning: The retained permutation of coordinates from resampling.
multiplication-algorithm.quote: Its exact counterpart $\mathscr F$ replaces each numerical routine by the exact map it approximates, so $\mathscr F=2^\gamma\mathcal B_0QF_{\boldsymbol t}\mathcal A=RF_{\boldsymbol s}$, where $R$ is a retained permutation of coordinates, not a scalar ring or row count.

multiplication-algorithm.name: computed opposite transform
multiplication-algorithm.meaning: The computed source transform with the opposite exponent sign.
multiplication-algorithm.quote: For an array $z$ (not a round input, an address suffix, an array acted on by a diagonal operator or a binary vector), the opposite-sign procedure is $\widetilde{\mathscr F}^{+}(z)=\overline{\widetilde{\mathscr F}(\overline z)}$; $R$ is real and conjugation flips the exponent sign, so its exact counterpart is $RF_{\boldsymbol s}^{+}$.

multiplication-algorithm.name: product array
multiplication-algorithm.meaning: The array given to the opposite transform: the truncated pointwise product of the two computed source transforms.
multiplication-algorithm.quote: For an array $z$ (not a round input, an address suffix, an array acted on by a diagonal operator or a binary vector), the opposite-sign procedure is $\widetilde{\mathscr F}^{+}(z)=\overline{\widetilde{\mathscr F}(\overline z)}$; $R$ is real and conjugation flips the exponent sign, so its exact counterpart is $RF_{\boldsymbol s}^{+}$.

multiplication-algorithm.name: source array
multiplication-algorithm.meaning: The first source array of grid values.
multiplication-algorithm.quote: Apply $\Phi$ to obtain source arrays $u,v$ (here arrays, not the input integers, a chunk width or binary vectors).

multiplication-algorithm.name: source array
multiplication-algorithm.meaning: The second source array of grid values.
multiplication-algorithm.quote: Apply $\Phi$ to obtain source arrays $u,v$ (here arrays, not the input integers, a chunk width or binary vectors).

multiplication-algorithm.name: scaled exact array
multiplication-algorithm.quote: Compute $\widetilde{\mathscr F}^{+}(z)$ and multiply by $S$, obtaining $\widetilde w$, which approximates the exact array $w=(u*v)/S$ (here $w$ is this scaled exact array, not a wire index, a summation index or a binary vector).

multiplication-algorithm.name: computed scaled array
multiplication-algorithm.meaning: The computed approximation of w after multiplying by S.
multiplication-algorithm.quote: Compute $\widetilde{\mathscr F}^{+}(z)$ and multiply by $S$, obtaining $\widetilde w$, which approximates the exact array $w=(u*v)/S$ (here $w$ is this scaled exact array, not a wire index, a summation index or a binary vector).

packed-bit-addition.name: control bit
packed-bit-addition.meaning: A control bit, equal to 0 or 1, that gates each addition.
packed-bit-addition.quote: For a control bit $c$ (not a scaling integer) and integers $u,w$ (not a DFT sequence, a chunk width or a wire index), $c[P]$ is $c$ if $P$ holds, else $0$.

packed-bit-addition.name: first integer
packed-bit-addition.meaning: One of the two integers whose parities the eight additions act on.
packed-bit-addition.quote: For a control bit $c$ (not a scaling integer) and integers $u,w$ (not a DFT sequence, a chunk width or a wire index), $c[P]$ is $c$ if $P$ holds, else $0$.

packed-bit-addition.name: second integer
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The other integer, an arbitrary auxiliary value that is restored.
packed-bit-addition.quote: For a control bit $c$ (not a scaling integer) and integers $u,w$ (not a DFT sequence, a chunk width or a wire index), $c[P]$ is $c$ if $P$ holds, else $0$.

packed-bit-addition.name: record bits
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The number of bits in the record stored at each address.
packed-bit-addition.quote: Each address holds an $R$-bit record ($R$ is neither the scalar ring nor a row count) and three chunks $x,y,z$ ($y$ is not the ring variable) of $L=fK$ bits ($L$ is not a dimension loss), with $K\ge6$ the segment spacing ($K$ is not a tensor line) and $f$ the number of selected bits; other coordinates are spectators.

packed-bit-addition.name: chunk width

packed-bit-addition.quote: Each address holds an $R$-bit record ($R$ is neither the scalar ring nor a row count) and three chunks $x,y,z$ ($y$ is not the ring variable) of $L=fK$ bits ($L$ is not a dimension loss), with $K\ge6$ the segment spacing ($K$ is not a tensor line) and $f$ the number of selected bits; other coordinates are spectators.

packed-bit-addition.name: selected-bit count
packed-bit-addition.quote: Each address holds an $R$-bit record ($R$ is neither the scalar ring nor a row count) and three chunks $x,y,z$ ($y$ is not the ring variable) of $L=fK$ bits ($L$ is not a dimension loss), with $K\ge6$ the segment spacing ($K$ is not a tensor line) and $f$ the number of selected bits; other coordinates are spectators.

packed-bit-addition.name: address count
packed-bit-addition.quote: Let $M$ count addresses ($M$ is not a vertex matrix), $V=MR$, and $A_{\rm rect}=\lceil\log_2(2V)\rceil$ bound counter lengths.

packed-bit-addition.name: array volume
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The total number of bits M times R.
packed-bit-addition.quote: Let $M$ count addresses ($M$ is not a vertex matrix), $V=MR$, and $A_{\rm rect}=\lceil\log_2(2V)\rceil$ bound counter lengths.

packed-bit-addition.name: counter length
packed-bit-addition.meaning: An upper bound on the bits of the counters, the ceiling of log2(2V).
packed-bit-addition.quote: Let $M$ count addresses ($M$ is not a vertex matrix), $V=MR$, and $A_{\rm rect}=\lceil\log_2(2V)\rceil$ bound counter lengths.

packed-bit-addition.name: offset
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The offset of the first selected position within a segment spacing.

packed-bit-addition.name: selected position

packed-bit-addition.name: packed map
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The composition of the eight packed cyclic shifts.

packed-bit-addition.name: ideal map
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The ideal permutation that performs the required XORs and fixes all other coordinates.

parameter-choice.quote: Put $\gamma=2d\alpha^2$ and $\eta=1/(4d)$, where $\gamma$ is the exponent of the scale factor $2^\gamma$ of $d$-axis resampling, and $\eta$ is the smallest relative distance at which a prime $s_i$ may lie below $t_i$.

parameter-choice.name: interval integer
parameter-choice.meaning: An integer in the prime-interval lemma, not a radix or sequence length.
parameter-choice.quote: In the prime-interval lemma below, $q$ is an integer, not a radix or a sequence length as on earlier pages.

parameter-choice.name: a_d constant
parameter-choice.meaning: Lower constant in the bound a_d p^epsilon <= d.
parameter-choice.quote: The lemmas assume $a_dp^\epsilon\le d\le b_dp^\epsilon$, $2^{a_rp/d}\le r\le2^{b_rp/d}$ and $d\ell\le C_\ell p$ for fixed constants $a_d,b_d,a_r,b_r,C_\ell$.

parameter-choice.name: b_d constant
parameter-choice.meaning: Upper constant in the bound d <= b_d p^epsilon.
parameter-choice.quote: The lemmas assume $a_dp^\epsilon\le d\le b_dp^\epsilon$, $2^{a_rp/d}\le r\le2^{b_rp/d}$ and $d\ell\le C_\ell p$ for fixed constants $a_d,b_d,a_r,b_r,C_\ell$.

parameter-choice.name: a_r constant
parameter-choice.meaning: Lower constant in the bound 2^(a_r p/d) <= r.
parameter-choice.quote: The lemmas assume $a_dp^\epsilon\le d\le b_dp^\epsilon$, $2^{a_rp/d}\le r\le2^{b_rp/d}$ and $d\ell\le C_\ell p$ for fixed constants $a_d,b_d,a_r,b_r,C_\ell$.

parameter-choice.name: b_r constant
parameter-choice.meaning: Upper constant in the bound r <= 2^(b_r p/d).
parameter-choice.quote: The lemmas assume $a_dp^\epsilon\le d\le b_dp^\epsilon$, $2^{a_rp/d}\le r\le2^{b_rp/d}$ and $d\ell\le C_\ell p$ for fixed constants $a_d,b_d,a_r,b_r,C_\ell$.

parameter-choice.name: C_ell constant
parameter-choice.meaning: Constant in the bound d ell <= C_ell p.
parameter-choice.quote: The lemmas assume $a_dp^\epsilon\le d\le b_dp^\epsilon$, $2^{a_rp/d}\le r\le2^{b_rp/d}$ and $d\ell\le C_\ell p$ for fixed constants $a_d,b_d,a_r,b_r,C_\ell$.

phase-frames.name: binary vector
phase-frames.meaning: A binary vector in F_2^m (not the number of triples).
phase-frames.quote: Here $v$ is a binary vector, not the number of triples on the exchange-network page.

phase-frames.name: edge residual
phase-frames.meaning: The edge residual of an edge: the orthogonal summand added going from U to V (not a tensor factor).
phase-frames.quote: Here $E$ is an edge residual, not the first tensor factor on the tensor-product page.

phase-frames.name: column count
phase-frames.meaning: The number of columns of data, so that an address is a k-tuple (not a depth).
phase-frames.quote: Here $k$ counts columns of data, not the depth on the fixed-point page.

phase-frames.name: binary vector
phase-frames.meaning: A binary vector in F_2^m (not an input sequence).
phase-frames.quote: Here $u$ is a binary vector, not the input sequence on the discrete Fourier transform page.

phase-frames.name: binary vector
phase-frames.quote: Labels are subspaces of $\mathbb F_2^m$ ($m$ the label dimension), and $u,v,w,z$ are vectors of $\mathbb F_2^m$ here.

phase-frames.name: binary vector
phase-frames.quote: Labels are subspaces of $\mathbb F_2^m$ ($m$ the label dimension), and $u,v,w,z$ are vectors of $\mathbb F_2^m$ here.

phase-frames.name: support
phase-frames.meaning: The set of coordinates where a binary vector is 1.
phase-frames.quote: The support $\operatorname{supp}(z)$ of a vector is the set of coordinates where it is $1$.

phase-frames.name: Hamming weight
phase-frames.meaning: The Hamming weight: the number of coordinates where a binary vector is 1.
phase-frames.quote: Write $\operatorname{wt}(x)=|\operatorname{supp}(x)|$ for the Hamming weight, $[b]\in\{0,1\}$ for the integer representative of $b\in\mathbb F_2$, $P_U$ for projection onto a label $U$, and $z\cdot w$ for the dot product, both over $\mathbb F_2$.

phase-frames.name: projection
phase-frames.meaning: The projection onto a label U over F_2.
phase-frames.quote: Write $\operatorname{wt}(x)=|\operatorname{supp}(x)|$ for the Hamming weight, $[b]\in\{0,1\}$ for the integer representative of $b\in\mathbb F_2$, $P_U$ for projection onto a label $U$, and $z\cdot w$ for the dot product, both over $\mathbb F_2$.

phase-frames.name: translation by v
phase-frames.meaning: The translation of functions of x by the binary vector v.
phase-frames.quote: Let $X_v$ be the translation $(X_vf)(x)=f(x+v)$, and $C=H\operatorname{diag}(1,i)H=aI+bX$ with $a=\frac{1+i}{2}$, $b=\frac{1-i}{2}$, where $H=\tfrac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$.

phase-frames.name: weight phase exponent
phase-frames.meaning: The Hamming weight of P_U x, modulo four.
phase-frames.quote: For a label $U$ put $q_U(x)=\operatorname{wt}(P_Ux)\bmod 4$, with the projection taken over $\mathbb F_2$.

phase-frames.name: phase frame
phase-frames.meaning: The phase frame of the label U.
phase-frames.quote: The phase frame is $\mathcal C_U=H^{\otimes m}\operatorname{diag}_x(i^{q_U(x)})H^{\otimes m}$, with Gaussian-dyadic entries.

phase-frames.name: orthonormal basis
phase-frames.meaning: An orthonormal basis of the edge residual E.
phase-frames.quote: Take an edge from $U$ to $V=U\perp E$, where $E$, the edge residual, has orthonormal basis $\mathcal B$.

phase-frames.name: edge phase sign
phase-frames.meaning: The sign, plus or minus one modulo four, of one basis vector's phase term, including the edge direction.
phase-frames.quote: Each term is therefore $\varepsilon[v\cdot x]$ with $\varepsilon=\pm1$ modulo four, the sign including the edge direction.

phase-frames.name: sign matrix
phase-frames.quote: With $Z=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$ we have $ZXZ=-X$ and $C^{-1}=bI+aX$; since $ib=a$ and $ia=-b$, $C=iZC^{-1}Z$.

phase-frames.name: sign operator
phase-frames.meaning: Z on the 27 coordinates of supp(u) in every column, the identity elsewhere.
phase-frames.quote: Let $Z_{a,k}$ be $Z$ on those 27 coordinates in every column.

phase-kernel.name: identity matrix
phase-kernel.quote: Let $I$ be the $2\times 2$ identity matrix, and let $X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ be the bit flip, which swaps the two entries of a pair $(u,v)$.

phase-kernel.name: bit flip
phase-kernel.meaning: The 2x2 matrix swapping the two entries of a pair.
phase-kernel.quote: Let $I$ be the $2\times 2$ identity matrix, and let $X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ be the bit flip, which swaps the two entries of a pair $(u,v)$.

phase-kernel.name: kernel constant
phase-kernel.quote: Let $a=\frac{1+i}{2}$ be a complex constant, which is not a bank index.

phase-kernel.name: kernel coefficient
phase-kernel.meaning: The complex coefficient (1-i)/2 of the bit flip in the kernel.
phase-kernel.quote: Let $b=\frac{1-i}{2}$ be the kernel coefficient, which here is not the lowest bit of the output index as on the butterfly page.

phase-kernel.name: phase matrix
phase-kernel.meaning: The diagonal matrix diag(1, i) multiplying the second entry of a pair by i.
phase-kernel.quote: Let $\mathsf S=\operatorname{diag}(1,i)$ be the phase matrix that multiplies the second entry of a pair by $i$.

phase-kernel.name: averaging step
phase-kernel.meaning: The matrix of the two-point averaging and differencing step.
phase-kernel.quote: Let $H_0=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$ be the matrix of the averaging and differencing step $(u,v)\mapsto\bigl(\tfrac{u+v}{2},\tfrac{u-v}{2}\bigr)$, and let $H=\sqrt2\,H_0$ be the normalized Hadamard matrix, which is symmetric and satisfies $H^2=I$.

phase-kernel.name: Hadamard matrix
phase-kernel.meaning: The normalized Hadamard matrix sqrt(2) H_0.
phase-kernel.quote: Let $H_0=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$ be the matrix of the averaging and differencing step $(u,v)\mapsto\bigl(\tfrac{u+v}{2},\tfrac{u-v}{2}\bigr)$, and let $H=\sqrt2\,H_0$ be the normalized Hadamard matrix, which is symmetric and satisfies $H^2=I$.

phase-twist.name: first array
phase-twist.meaning: The first complex array being convolved.
phase-twist.quote: Let $f$ and $g$ be two complex arrays with $d$ axes, the last of length $r$, and $T$ entries in all.

phase-twist.name: second array
phase-twist.meaning: The second complex array being convolved with f.
phase-twist.quote: Let $f$ and $g$ be two complex arrays with $d$ axes, the last of length $r$, and $T$ entries in all.

phase-twist.name: axis count
phase-twist.meaning: The number of axes of the arrays.
phase-twist.quote: Let $f$ and $g$ be two complex arrays with $d$ axes, the last of length $r$, and $T$ entries in all.

phase-twist.name: last-axis variable
phase-twist.meaning: The variable of the last cyclic axis.
phase-twist.quote: Convolution along the last axis is multiplication in $\mathbb C[x_d]/(x_d^r-1)$, where $x_d$ is the variable of that axis.

phase-twist.name: negacyclic ring
phase-twist.meaning: The ring of polynomials modulo y^r+1.
phase-twist.quote: The twist converts the last cyclic axis into the coordinate of the [Polynomial ring modulo y^r + 1](ring-y.md), written $\mathcal R_r$, where $y^r=-1$ instead.

phase-twist.name: twist root
phase-twist.meaning: The primitive 2r-th root of unity e^{\pi i/r}, with zeta^r=-1.

phase-twist.name: twist map
phase-twist.meaning: The ring isomorphism from the cyclic ring to the negacyclic ring sending x_d to zeta y.
phase-twist.quote: Define the ring map $\Theta$ from $\mathbb C[x_d]/(x_d^r-1)$ to $\mathcal R_r$ by $x_d\mapsto\zeta y$.

phase-twist.name: coefficient index
phase-twist.meaning: An index of a coefficient (not an operation count).
phase-twist.quote: Here $k$ and $l$ index coefficients, not operations.

phase-twist.name: second coefficient index
phase-twist.meaning: An index of a coefficient of the second factor.
phase-twist.quote: Here $k$ and $l$ index coefficients, not operations.

phase-twist.name: wrapped position
phase-twist.meaning: The position k+l reduced modulo r.
phase-twist.quote: Take $k,l<r$ and write $k+l=j+hr$, with $j<r$ the resulting position and $h\in\{0,1\}$ the wrap indicator.

phase-twist.name: wrap indicator
phase-twist.meaning: Zero or one according to whether k+l wrapped past r.
phase-twist.quote: Take $k,l<r$ and write $k+l=j+hr$, with $j<r$ the resulting position and $h\in\{0,1\}$ the wrap indicator.

phase-twist.name: record reading
phase-twist.meaning: The map reading each line along the last axis as a polynomial in R_r.
phase-twist.quote: $\iota$ reads each line $(f_{\boldsymbol j,k})_k$ as the polynomial $\sum_k f_{\boldsymbol j,k}y^k$, giving an array of $M$ records in $\mathcal R_r$.

phase-twist.name: diagonal twist
phase-twist.meaning: The maps multiplying entry k of each line by zeta^{+-k}.
phase-twist.quote: Let $(D_\pm f)_{\boldsymbol j,k}=\zeta^{\pm k}f_{\boldsymbol j,k}$ multiply entry $k$ of each line by $\zeta^{\pm k}$.

phase-twist.name: ring convolution
phase-twist.meaning: Normalized convolution of the first d-1 axes over R_r, including division by T.
phase-twist.quote: Let $\mathcal M_r$ be the ring convolution of [Convolution from the retained transform layout](ring-convolution.md): it convolves the first $d-1$ axes over $\mathcal R_r$, dividing by $T$.

phase-twist.name: complex convolution
phase-twist.meaning: The normalized complex cyclic convolution of two arrays.
phase-twist.quote: The composite $\mathcal M_{\mathbb C}$, the normalized complex cyclic convolution, is

phase-twist.name: sup norm
phase-twist.meaning: The largest modulus of a scalar coefficient of f.
phase-twist.quote: Write $\|f\|$ for the sup norm of an array $f$: the largest modulus of a scalar coefficient.

precision-recovery.name: grid spacing
precision-recovery.meaning: The grid spacing 2^{-p} of the fixed-point records.
precision-recovery.quote: Write $h_p=2^{-p}$ and $L=\log_2T$, the base-2 logarithm of the padded length $T$ (the letter $L$ here is not a linear map as on the contractions page).

precision-recovery.name: log of padded length
precision-recovery.meaning: The base-2 logarithm of the padded length T.
precision-recovery.quote: Write $h_p=2^{-p}$ and $L=\log_2T$, the base-2 logarithm of the padded length $T$ (the letter $L$ here is not a linear map as on the contractions page).

precision-recovery.name: error size
precision-recovery.meaning: The size of an error in grid spacings.
precision-recovery.quote: Norms are sup norms, an error of $a$ means error below $ah_p$ (here $a$ is an error size in grid spacings, not the chirp), and every array stays in the unit disk (norm $\le1$).

precision-recovery.name: disk array
precision-recovery.meaning: An array in the unit disk to which a phase or chirp transform is applied.
precision-recovery.quote: For a unit phase $e$, an approximation $\widetilde e$ with $|\widetilde e-e|<2h_p$ and a disk operand $x$ (here $x$ is an array in the unit disk to which a phase or chirp transform is applied, not the polynomial variable), the product differs by under $2\|x\|h_p$ and truncation $Q_p$ adds under $\sqrt2h_p$, so $\|Q_p(\widetilde ex)-ex\|<(2\|x\|+\sqrt2)h_p<4h_p$.

precision-recovery.name: scaled first digits
precision-recovery.meaning: The scaled digit array of the first input.
precision-recovery.quote: Now $u,v$ are the scaled digit arrays of the two inputs, not the input integers of the radix-digit page: each digit is stored as its value times $2^{-b-2}$, so norms are below $1/4$.

precision-recovery.name: scaled second digits
precision-recovery.meaning: The scaled digit array of the second input.
precision-recovery.quote: Now $u,v$ are the scaled digit arrays of the two inputs, not the input integers of the radix-digit page: each digit is stored as its value times $2^{-b-2}$, so norms are below $1/4$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: first input
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The first of the two n-bit integers being multiplied.

radix-digit-reduction.name: second input
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The second of the two n-bit integers being multiplied (not the number of triples).

radix-digit-reduction.name: digit bits
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The number of bits in one radix-2^b digit.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Let $n$ be the number of bits in each input, and let $b=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$ be the number of bits in one digit, so $n\le 2^b$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: padded length
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The padded length, a power of two with 4n/b <= T < 8n/b.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: $T$ is the padded length, a power of two with $4n/b\le T<8n/b$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: convolution length
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The length of the cyclic convolution, with T/2<S<T.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: $S$ is the length of the cyclic convolution, a product of distinct odd primes with $T/2<S<T$.

radix-digit-reduction.name: digit count
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The number of digits in each input, not the sequence length of the convolution page.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Let $q=\lceil n/b\rceil$ be the number of digits in each input, padding with leading zeros; on this page $q$ is the digit count, not the length of the sequences being convolved as on the convolution page.

radix-digit-reduction.name: polynomial variable
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The indeterminate of the digit polynomials, evaluated at 2^b to recover the integers.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Let $x$ be a polynomial variable, and form the polynomials in $x$ with the $u_i$ and with the $v_k$ as coefficients.

radix-digit-reduction.name: product coefficient
radix-digit-reduction.meaning: The coefficient of x^j in the product of the two digit polynomials.
radix-digit-reduction.quote: Let $c_j=\sum_{i+k=j}u_iv_k$ be the coefficient of $x^j$ in that product.

rank-recurrence.name: call parameter
rank-recurrence.meaning: The parameter of a recursive call: the number of digits per interchanged chunk, or the number of selected axes of a layer.
rank-recurrence.quote: A call acts on a stream of volume $V$ and has a parameter $f$ (a number here, not an array): the digits per interchanged chunk, or the selected axes of a layer.

rank-recurrence.name: time per unit volume
rank-recurrence.meaning: The running time of a call at a given parameter, divided by the volume of its stream.
rank-recurrence.quote: Let $\mathcal C(f)$ be the time per unit volume at parameter $f$: the running time of a call at parameter $f$, divided by the volume of its stream.

rank-recurrence.name: recursion depth
rank-recurrence.meaning: The number of recursion levels below the top call, indexing the terms of the unrolled sum; here not the stage number of the subspace-labels page.
rank-recurrence.quote: Here $j$ means the recursion depth, the number of levels below the top call, not the stage number as on [Nested subspace labels and rank deficit](subspace-labels.md): unrolling $\log_m f$ levels, depth $j$ contributes $(s/W)^j$, so $\mathcal C(f)=O\big(\sum_{j=0}^{\log_m f}(s/W)^j\big)$.

rank-recurrence.name: relative rank deficit
rank-recurrence.meaning: The relative deficit (Wm-s)/(Wm) by which the number of smaller calls falls short of Wm.
rank-recurrence.quote: Write $s/W=m(1-\eta)$, with $\eta$ now the relative deficit $(Wm-s)/(Wm)$.

retained-permutations.name: unit
retained-permutations.meaning: A unit modulo q, an integer coprime to q, used as the multiplier of the index permutation R_beta.
retained-permutations.quote: For a unit $\beta$ modulo $q$, let $(R_\beta z)_j=z_{\beta j}$.

retained-permutations.name: index scaling
retained-permutations.meaning: The permutation of a length-q vector sending z to the vector with entries z_{beta j}.
retained-permutations.quote: For a unit $\beta$ modulo $q$, let $(R_\beta z)_j=z_{\beta j}$.

retained-permutations.name: summation index
retained-permutations.meaning: The index of the sum defining the transform of R_beta z.
retained-permutations.quote: Then $(F_q^+R_\beta z)_j=\frac1q\sum_w z_{\beta w}e^{2\pi i wj/q}$, where $w$ is the summation index.

retained-permutations.name: new summation index
retained-permutations.meaning: The summation index after the substitution w' = beta w.
retained-permutations.quote: Substituting $w'=\beta w$, with $w'$ the new summation index, gives $\frac1q\sum_{w'}z_{w'}e^{2\pi i w'\beta^{-1}j/q}$, which is $(R_\beta^{-1}F_q^+z)_j$.

retained-permutations.name: setup degree
retained-permutations.meaning: A fixed exponent such that setup work per line is O(p^nu).
retained-permutations.quote:
Since $t_i\ge r/2$, each tensor map invokes at most $\sum_iT/t_i\le 2dT/r$ lines, so setup work $O(p^
u)$ per line, with $
u$ a fixed exponent, totals $O(dTp^
u/r)$.

retained-permutations.name: opposite transform
retained-permutations.meaning: The discrete Fourier transform of length q with the sign of the exponent reversed.
retained-permutations.quote: For a vector $z$ of $q$ complex entries, the normalized [discrete Fourier transform](dft.md) is $(F_qz)_k=\frac1q\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}z_je^{-2\pi ijk/q}$, and $F_q^+$, the opposite transform, is the same with the exponent's sign reversed.

retained-permutations.name: transformed vector
retained-permutations.meaning: A vector of q complex entries.
retained-permutations.quote: For a vector $z$ of $q$ complex entries, the normalized [discrete Fourier transform](dft.md) is $(F_qz)_k=\frac1q\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}z_je^{-2\pi ijk/q}$, and $F_q^+$, the opposite transform, is the same with the exponent's sign reversed.

retained-permutations.name: axis input contraction
retained-permutations.meaning: The linear contraction applied to the input of one axis in the resampling identity.
retained-permutations.quote: That page gives linear contractions $A$, $B_0$ ($B_0$ is not the packing base) with $P_sF_s=2^{2\alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA$, computed in time $O(tp^{3/2+\delta}\alpha)$ without executing $P_s$ or $P_t$.

retained-permutations.name: axis output contraction
retained-permutations.meaning: The linear contraction applied to the output of one axis in the resampling identity.
retained-permutations.quote: That page gives linear contractions $A$, $B_0$ ($B_0$ is not the packing base) with $P_sF_s=2^{2\alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA$, computed in time $O(tp^{3/2+\delta}\alpha)$ without executing $P_s$ or $P_t$.

retained-permutations.name: source permutation
retained-permutations.meaning: The permutation (P_s u)_j = u_{tj} of a length-s vector.
retained-permutations.quote: For one axis, with $p$, $\alpha$, $\delta$ as there, let $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$ ($u,v$ are complex arrays here, not integers).

retained-permutations.name: target permutation
retained-permutations.meaning: The permutation (P_t v)_k = v_{-sk} of a length-t vector.
retained-permutations.quote: For one axis, with $p$, $\alpha$, $\delta$ as there, let $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$ ($u,v$ are complex arrays here, not integers).

retained-permutations.name: first array
retained-permutations.meaning: A complex array, not an integer here.
retained-permutations.quote: For one axis, with $p$, $\alpha$, $\delta$ as there, let $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$ ($u,v$ are complex arrays here, not integers).

retained-permutations.name: second array
retained-permutations.meaning: A complex array, not an integer here.
retained-permutations.quote: For one axis, with $p$, $\alpha$, $\delta$ as there, let $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$ ($u,v$ are complex arrays here, not integers).

ring-convolution.name: pointwise product
ring-convolution.meaning: The pointwise product P(u,v)=uv/r of two arrays over the ring.
ring-convolution.quote: Write $P(u,v)=uv/r$ for the pointwise product; here $P$ means this product, not the number of prefix values of the stream-operations page, the earlier tensor line of the subspace-labels page, or a subspace of $A$ as on the tensor-product page.

ring-convolution.name: layout permutation
ring-convolution.meaning: The permutation of records defined by the tape layout of the transforms.
ring-convolution.quote: Perform both forward transforms and retain their common $LB$ order, with $L$ the layout permutation of records (here not the linear map of the contraction page, nor the total dimension loss of the subspace-labels page) and $B$ the bit-reversal order (here not the row length of the stream-operations page, the suffix digit count of the controlled-shifts page, or an orthogonal complement as on the subspace-labels and tensor-product pages).

ring-convolution.name: bit-reversal order
ring-convolution.meaning: The bit-reversal order applied along every axis.
ring-convolution.quote: Perform both forward transforms and retain their common $LB$ order, with $L$ the layout permutation of records (here not the linear map of the contraction page, nor the total dimension loss of the subspace-labels page) and $B$ the bit-reversal order (here not the row length of the stream-operations page, the suffix digit count of the controlled-shifts page, or an orthogonal complement as on the subspace-labels and tensor-product pages).

ring-convolution.name: truncation error bound
ring-convolution.meaning: The bound sqrt2 times 2^{-p} on the change made by truncation to p fractional bits.
ring-convolution.quote: Each record product is formed by [Signed packing](signed-packing.md) in $O(rp\log(rp))$ time, truncated by $Q_p$ to $p$ bits of precision, which changes it by less than $\eta=\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$ (here $\eta$ is a truncation error bound, not the relative rank deficit of the recursive power saving page) without raising the norm.

ring-y.name: ring variable
ring-y.meaning: The indeterminate of the polynomials; it satisfies y^r = -1 in the ring.
ring-y.quote: Write $\mathcal R_r=\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ for it, where $y$ is the ring variable, the indeterminate of the polynomials, and $r$ is the record length, the number of complex coefficients in a polynomial of the ring, always a power of two with $r\geq 2$.

ring-y.name: record length
ring-y.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in a polynomial of the ring, always a power of two.
ring-y.quote: Write $\mathcal R_r=\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ for it, where $y$ is the ring variable, the indeterminate of the polynomials, and $r$ is the record length, the number of complex coefficients in a polynomial of the ring, always a power of two with $r\geq 2$.

signed-packing.name: packing base
signed-packing.meaning: The base 2^{4p} at which the polynomials are evaluated.

signed-packing.name: signed evaluation integer
signed-packing.meaning: The integer obtained by evaluating the integer-coefficient polynomial u at B_0.
signed-packing.quote: let $A_u=u(B_0)=\sum_{j<r}u_jB_0^j$ be the signed evaluation integer

signed-packing.name: carry
signed-packing.meaning: The carry, in {-1,0}, into block j when forming A_u.
signed-packing.quote: scan the coefficients with a carry $\gamma_j$

signed-packing.name: block
signed-packing.meaning: The residue of u_j plus the carry modulo B_0, the j-th block of 4p bits of A_u.
signed-packing.quote: Let $d_j\in[0,B_0)$ be the residue of $u_j+\gamma_j$ modulo $B_0$

signed-packing.name: product coefficient
signed-packing.meaning: The coefficient of y^j in the ordinary product h=ac of integer polynomials.

signed-packing.name: extraction carry
signed-packing.meaning: The carry into block j during extraction, in {0,1}.
signed-packing.quote: let $\rho_j$ be the carry into block $j$

signed-packing.name: reduced coefficient
signed-packing.meaning: The Gaussian integer coefficient of y^j after reduction modulo y^r+1.
signed-packing.quote: Let $H_j$ be the resulting Gaussian integer coefficient.

simultaneous-layer.name: selected chunk count
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The number of selected address chunks.
simultaneous-layer.quote: The simultaneous butterfly layer applies $H_0$ coefficientwise to one bit of each of $D\le d$ selected address chunks of $K$ bits, at a common offset, in time $O(Vd^{\lambda'}),$ $\lambda'<1,$ instead of $D$ passes; here $D$ is the number of selected address chunks, not the second chunk value of [Fast address-chunk interchange](address-interchange.md), and $D$ is not the source group of [Matrix shear by triangular factorization](matrix-shear.md).

simultaneous-layer.name: selected axis count
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The number of selected axes in a group.
simultaneous-layer.quote: A group of $e=mf$ selected axes ($e$ is the number of selected axes, not the number of digits in a chunk as on [Fast address-chunk interchange](address-interchange.md)) has $m$ slots of $f$ axes; a column holds one bit per slot, in $\mathbb F_2^m.$

simultaneous-layer.name: array
simultaneous-layer.meaning: An array acted on by the diagonal operator.
simultaneous-layer.quote: where the diagonal operator $\mathcal S_D$ acts on an array $z$ by $(\mathcal S_Dz)(x)=i^{x_1+\dots+x_D}z(x).$

simultaneous-layer.name: diagonal phase operator
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The diagonal operator multiplying the value at address x by i to the sum of the selected bits.
simultaneous-layer.quote: where the diagonal operator $\mathcal S_D$ acts on an array $z$ by $(\mathcal S_Dz)(x)=i^{x_1+\dots+x_D}z(x).$

simultaneous-layer.name: basis-change matrix
simultaneous-layer.meaning: An invertible F_2 matrix whose first columns are the residual basis vectors.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Let $\Gamma$ be an invertible $\mathbb F_2$-matrix with first columns $v_\xi$ and $\mathcal P_\Gamma:x\mapsto\Gamma x$ an address permutation.

simultaneous-layer.name: address permutation
simultaneous-layer.meaning: The address permutation moving the value at x to Gamma x.
simultaneous-layer.quote: Let $\Gamma$ be an invertible $\mathbb F_2$-matrix with first columns $v_\xi$ and $\mathcal P_\Gamma:x\mapsto\Gamma x$ an address permutation.

simultaneous-layer.name: residual basis index

simultaneous-layer.quote: with residual basis vectors $v_\xi$ indexed by $\xi,$ $\eta_\xi=\pm1,$ $C_v=aI+bX_v$ and $X_v$ shifting a column by $v.$

simultaneous-layer.name: edge sign

simultaneous-layer.quote: with residual basis vectors $v_\xi$ indexed by $\xi,$ $\eta_\xi=\pm1,$ $C_v=aI+bX_v$ and $X_v$ shifting a column by $v.$

simultaneous-layer.name: standard basis vector

simultaneous-layer.name: individual chunk count

transform-layout.name: transformed axis count

address-interchange.quote: So the time per unit volume $F_k$ at width $m^k$ obeys $F_0=O(1)$, $F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1)$, the recurrence of [Recursive power saving](rank-recurrence.md).
The interchange performs each edge shear by [Matrix shear by triangular factorization](matrix-shear.md): if $A_i$ has rank $a$, then $\Phi_{A_i}$ costs $a$ interchanges of $b$-digit fields
Rows are split into role streams by [Elementary stream operations](stream-ops.md)

array-frames.quote: They extend the [linear exchange network with restored scratch wires](exchange-network.md) from scalars to arrays while keeping each edge cheap.

butterfly.quote: Repeated over the address bits of an array, with twiddle multiplications between layers, it computes the [Discrete Fourier transform](dft.md) of an array in $\log_2 t$ layers instead of $t^2$ operations.

chirp.quote: The Bluestein chirp identity rewrites a permuted [Discrete Fourier transform](dft.md) as a pointwise chirp phase, a cyclic convolution, and another chirp phase, so the target permutation of resampling is absorbed into the convolution and never executed as a sort.
The permuted transform is thus reduced to one [Cyclic convolution](convolution.md) of length $T$ between two pointwise phase multiplications.

conjecture.quote: The conjecture is stated for the [Fixed finite-tape machine model](machine-model.md): a multitape Turing machine with a fixed alphabet and a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes.

controlled-shifts.quote: Each operation below is carried out by splitting into streams and merging back, as in [Elementary stream operations](stream-ops.md).

cost-accounting.quote: Cost accounting totals the running time of every step of [The multiplication algorithm](multiplication-algorithm.md) and shows that it is $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$, where $\kappa=2^{-182}$ is the saved exponent.
The layout needs $O(p/K)$ chunk exchanges, as $d\ell=O(p)$, each costing $O(VK^\tau)$ by [Fast address-chunk interchange](address-interchange.md).
Each of at most $\ell$ rounds costs $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ by [Simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-layer.md).
Exceptional addresses, where the packed shifts of [Packed selected-bit addition](packed-bit-addition.md) fail, are bounded to a fraction $O(d2^{-K})$ of addresses.

crt-map.quote: Hence $\Phi$ is an isomorphism and preserves [Cyclic convolution](convolution.md).
The map is implemented by these shifts, each of linear cost by [Controlled shifts and rational scalings](controlled-shifts.md).

dft.quote: The transform diagonalizes [cyclic convolution](convolution.md): the transform of a convolution is a pointwise product of transforms.

exchange-network.quote: In the complex construction the network keeps its scalars in $\mathbb Z[i,1/2]$, the values of [Fixed-point Gaussian dyadic records](fixed-point.md), and the neighbours of a triple are the distinct triples with even intersection (zero or two).

fixed-point.quote: A record is laid out on the tapes of the [Fixed finite-tape machine model](machine-model.md) as $2r$ consecutive fixed-width integers, so it is read and moved by ordinary tape scans.

frequency-order.quote: It orders the outputs of the [synthetic polynomial transform](synthetic-transform.md) over $\mathcal R_r=\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$, normed by the largest coefficient modulus.

gaussian-resampling.quote: Here $F_q$ is the normalised [Discrete Fourier transform](dft.md) of length $q$, and the resampling re-expresses $F_s$ through $F_t$.
